headline.technical: Bloomberg reported Wall Street flipped from AI euphoria to gloom; the S&P 500 is -6.99% over 1m, the Nasdaq Composite -10.92%, and the VIX closed at 26.80.
headline.layman: Bloomberg says Wall Street's mood on AI turned gloomy. The S&P 500 is down 6.99% in a month, though Asian shares rose on Friday.

global.title: AI worries and Fed rate-hike bets weigh on markets

status.technical: Bloomberg reported Wall Street flipped from AI euphoria to gloom. S&P 500 1m -6.99%, Nasdaq Composite 1m -10.92%; VIX closed 26.80. Reuters reported shares found footing after a bruising month, with the dollar set for a third monthly gain.
status.layman: Investors have turned nervous about AI stocks. The Nasdaq is down 10.92% in a month. Reuters says shares have steadied a little, while the US dollar is set for a third monthly gain.

consequence.technical: If AI-trade doubts persist alongside Fed rate rises (FT: Fed to press ahead with rate rises), equities could stay volatile. Mint links the AI-trade rupture and rising rates to safe-haven dollar demand. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: If worries about AI and higher interest rates continue, share prices may keep swinging. Mint says this mix is pushing investors toward safe places like the dollar.

impact.technical: Mint says the dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years; the US Dollar Index closed 103.75. The Nasdaq is most exposed to AI doubts, with a drawdown from 52w high of -14.54%. Evidence on other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Tech-focused investors feel it most: the Nasdaq sits 14.54% below its 52-week high. The dollar has been strengthening. The notes say little about other groups, so evidence is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 845 times (median 0.09%) and over the next 5 days 59% of 844 times (median 0.37%).
outlook.layman: History is a guide, not a forecast. After calm days like this, the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of the time and over the next five days 59% of the time.

regions.title: Americas: US tech steadies, Brazil jumps

status.technical: Straits Times: Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended down but well off lows. S&P 500 1d -0.25%, Dow 0.33%, Nasdaq -0.62%. Bloomberg reported Brazilian assets rallied after a banker was named finance minister; Bovespa 1d 6.07%, IPC 1d -1.43%.
status.layman: US shares ended slightly lower but well above their lows. Brazil's stock market rose 6.07% in a day after President Lula picked a well-known banker as finance minister.

consequence.technical: If the tech rebound reported by the FT holds, US sentiment could steady. FT framed Brazil's appointment as an attempt to calm markets after a sell-off. Base rate: after big rises Bovespa rose the next day 54% of 191 times. Not a prediction.
consequence.layman: If tech keeps recovering, US markets may calm. Brazil shows how fast markets can react to one appointment, made to calm markets after a sell-off.

impact.technical: Bloomberg: Banxico raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.9% from 1.5% on stronger exports and investment, yet the IPC fell 1.43% on the day. Brazilian assets gained on the finance-minister news. Evidence on US sectors beyond tech is thin.
impact.layman: Mexico's central bank raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.9% from 1.5%. Brazilian investors gained on the appointment. The notes say little about other US sectors.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose next day 54% of 845 times; after big rises the Bovespa rose next day 54% of 191 times (median 0.08%) and over the next 5 days 51% of 191 times (median 0.26%).
outlook.layman: History is only a guide. After calm days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of the time. After big jumps Brazil's Bovespa rose the next day 54% of the time.

regions.title: Europe: stocks rally as tariff worries ease

status.layman: European shares rose on Thursday. Yahoo Finance says worries about US tariffs eased. Germany's DAX rose 2.08% and Britain's FTSE 100 rose 1.75%.

consequence.technical: If tariff worries stay subdued, as the Yahoo Finance reports suggest, the rally could extend. Base rate: after big rises the DAX rose over the next 5 days 57% of 195 times. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: If tariff worries stay quiet, European shares could hold their gains. History only gives odds, not promises.

impact.technical: Straits Times: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 positions in AI restructuring; SAP closed -0.14% on the day. The ECB deposit facility rate is 2.5 %, previous 2.25. Evidence on other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Software firm SAP is weighing at least 10,000 job cuts as it restructures around AI. The European Central Bank's deposit rate is 2.5 %. The notes say little about other sectors.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: shares rise after tech rout

status.technical: Al Jazeera: indices in Japan, South Korea, Australia and Hong Kong rose after an earlier tech rout. Nikkei 225 1d 1.96%, KOSPI 3.80%, the Australian index 0.83%, Hang Seng 0.85%, Nifty 50 -0.43%. Economic Times: MSCI Asia Pacific gauge rose 0.6%.
status.layman: Most Asian stock markets rose after an earlier tech sell-off. Japan's Nikkei rose 1.96% and South Korea's KOSPI rose 3.80%. India's Nifty 50 slipped 0.43%.

consequence.technical: If AI sentiment stays stable, as WSJ reported on Friday, tech-linked Asian markets could keep recovering. But KOSPI is -17.64% over 1m with 20-day volatility of 58.3%, so large swings remain possible.
consequence.layman: If AI worries keep easing, Asian tech-linked markets could keep recovering. Swings are still large: South Korea's KOSPI is down 17.64% in a month.

impact.technical: CNBC: China's industrial profit growth hit a 5-month high of 20.1% in October, driven by AI-related manufacturing and exports while household consumption lagged. Straits Times: Tokyo inflation backs the case for a Bank of Japan rate hike; Ueda speaks Nov 30.
impact.layman: China's factory profits grew 20.1% in October, led by AI-related exports, while household spending lagged. Faster inflation in Tokyo strengthens the case for a Japanese rate rise.

drivers.title: Fed rate-hike expectations and a strong dollar

status.technical: FT: Fed to press ahead with rate rises. Economic Times reported forecasts point to a possible hike next month and that the dollar index reached a 22-month peak this week. The US Dollar Index closed 103.75, 1m 1.52%; the US 10-year yield closed 4.85.
status.layman: The Financial Times says the Fed will keep raising interest rates, and a hike may come next month. The US dollar hit a 22-month high this week and has strengthened over the past month.

consequence.technical: StoneX said a hawkish Fed sets a high bar for a durable gold recovery (WSJ). If hikes proceed, the dollar and yields could stay firm; gold closed 3664.20 with 3m -19.11%. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: If the Fed keeps raising rates, the dollar may stay strong. StoneX says that makes a lasting gold recovery harder. Gold is down 19.11% over three months.

impact.technical: Kitco reported gold slipped in holiday trading as Fed hike expectations persisted; gold 1d 3.63%. Investors in gold and dollar-sensitive assets are most affected. Evidence on other groups is thin.
impact.layman: People holding gold are affected most, since gold has fallen a lot recently. The notes say little about other groups, so evidence is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the US Dollar Index rose the next day 51% of 824 times (median 0.01%) and over the next 5 days 51% of 822 times (median 0.03%).
outlook.layman: History is a guide, not a forecast. After calm days the dollar index rose the next day about 51% of the time.

drivers.title: Oil and Middle East supply risk

status.technical: Economic Times: Brent trades near the month's high as Mideast conflict threatens supply, citing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and assaults on Saudi energy infrastructure. Investing.com: WTI jumped 2.5%. Brent closed 92.27 (1d -2.47%); WTI 85.79 (1d 2.52%).
status.layman: Oil is near this month's high because of conflict in the Middle East. Ships were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy sites were hit. WTI rose 2.52% in a day.

consequence.technical: If attacks on energy infrastructure continue (ANZ cited rising attacks, per WSJ), supply fears could keep oil elevated. Base rate: after look-alike days Brent rose over the next 5 days 1 of 5 times (median -6.19%). Not a prediction.
consequence.layman: If attacks on energy sites go on, oil prices could stay high. History shows prices often cooled after similar days, but that is not a promise.

impact.technical: Investing.com: Asia FX weakened as high oil prices weighed. Oil-importing economies and consumers face the cost; Brent is up 51.64% year to date. Al Jazeera reported an attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery killed one person.
impact.layman: High oil prices weigh on currencies in Asia and on fuel costs. Brent is up 51.64% so far this year. An attack on a Saudi refinery killed one person.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days Brent rose the next day 53% of 847 times (median 0.14%) and over the next 5 days 51% of 845 times (median 0.11%).
outlook.layman: History is only a guide. After calm days Brent rose the next day 53% of the time.

drivers.title: The AI trade: wobble and partial rebound

status.technical: Bloomberg: Wall Street flipped from AI euphoria to gloom; its Nov 26 wrap said Nasdaq futures climbed as the AI trade rebounded. WSJ: AI-linked exports and investment still drive Asian growth for now. Nvidia -3.91% 1d; Broadcom -15.02% 5d.
status.layman: AI stocks have swung from excitement to worry and back. WSJ says AI still drives growth in Asia for now. Nvidia fell 3.91% in a day and Broadcom is down 15.02% over five days.

consequence.technical: If worries about the AI boom's sustainability persist, tech selloffs could recur; Mint noted a brutal Kioxia selloff has made it Japan's cheapest blue chip, backing bullish analysts. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: If doubts about the AI boom last, tech shares could keep falling. Some analysts see bargains after the sell-off.

impact.technical: Nasdaq Composite drawdown from 52w high is -14.54%. Tech-heavy investors and AI-linked Asian exporters are most exposed; the notes give little on other groups, so evidence is thin.
impact.layman: Tech-heavy investors and AI-linked exporters feel it most. The Nasdaq is 14.54% below its 52-week high. The notes say little about others.

status.layman: Prices are rising faster in Tokyo, so investors expect Japan's central bank to raise interest rates. Its governor speaks on Nov 30 ahead of a Dec 18 decision.

consequence.layman: If Japan raises rates, banks may not gain as much as hoped, because competition and funding costs eat into profits, says Mint.

impact.layman: Japanese banks and bond investors are affected most. The notes say little about others, so evidence is thin.

drivers.title: China: strong factory profits, weak consumers

status.technical: CNBC: China's industrial profit growth surged to a 5-month high of 20.1% in October, with AI-related manufacturing and exports powering growth while household consumption lagged. WSJ: China extended its suspension of some critical-material export curbs to the U.S. until January.
status.layman: China's factory profits grew 20.1% in October thanks to AI-related exports, but households are spending less. China also paused some export limits on key materials to the US until January.

consequence.technical: An analyst note says China's property debt crisis is entering a new phase with developers at risk of defaulting again. If consumption stays weak, growth stays reliant on exports. Base rates are not predictions.
consequence.layman: Analysts say China's property problems are entering a new phase. If households keep spending less, growth leans on exports.

impact.technical: Shanghai Composite is -12.15% year to date and Shenzhen Component -23.83%. Export-linked tech firms are favoured per the notes; households and property developers face pressure. Evidence is thin beyond that.
impact.layman: China's stock markets are down this year: Shanghai by 12.15%, Shenzhen by 23.83%. Exporters are doing better than households and property firms.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Shanghai Composite rose the next day 51% of 843 times (median 0.02%) and over the next 5 days 51% of 840 times (median 0.05%).
outlook.layman: History is a guide, not a forecast. After calm days Shanghai rose the next day about 51% of the time.
